# andata-2

> andata-2 is a 4-track video live looper that runs in the browser: a video groovebox and sampler for live audiovisual performance. Record four webcam + microphone clips into banks, shape them, sequence them with a 16-step sequencer, perform them as a split-screen composition, and export the result as MP4. Free and open source; nothing is uploaded.

## What it is for

- Live audiovisual performance and VJ-style sets built from your own camera footage
- Making beat-synced split-screen music videos without a video editor
- Sketching loop-based music where every sound is also a picture

## Workflow

1. Record: pick a camera and mic, choose bank 1–4, record a clip (video + audio, encoded to MP4 in the browser via WebCodecs and mediabunny).
2. Shape: per bank — trim start/end, gain, pan, ADSR amplitude envelope, choke (retrigger cuts vs. overlaps), and video effects (two-tone gradient map, crush: pixelate X/Y and colour bit depth).
3. Sequence: 16-step grid at a set BPM; per-row mute; randomize and clear.
4. Perform: playing banks are composited live — 1 full frame, 2 side by side (stacked in vertical), 3 as two over one, 4 as a 2×2 grid — in 16:9 or 9:16. Audio is mixed through a master bus with a stereo meter.
5. Bounce: record the composed stage (picture + sound) and download it as MP4.

## Requirements

- A Chromium-based browser (Chrome, Edge, Arc) with WebCodecs and Web Audio
- Camera and microphone permission; served over HTTPS or localhost
- Headphones recommended while recording
